title: Functional programming books overview
publication_date: First published in the first issue of the Russian magazine "Practice of functional programming"; page last updated September 4, 2017
abstract: Functional programming has very long history and a lot of books was released in paper & electronic forms. These books covers all areas, from theoretical foundations of functional programming to programming in concrete languages & frameworks.
summary:
The page is an HTML bibliographic overview rather than a conventional research paper. It organizes books on functional programming into theoretical foundations, type and category theory, language implementation, cross-language introductions, and individual languages including Haskell, Erlang, OCaml, F#, Standard ML, Lisp, Scheme, Prolog, Scala, and Clojure. It also provides reading recommendations for learning functional programming and selected languages. ([alexott.net](https://alexott.net/en/fp/books/))

Evidence of influence is limited to reuse as a curated educational resource and reading-list entry. The overview has been listed by programming-languages reading resources, including the PLS Lab's collection of classic programming-language materials, Papers We Love, and functional-programming resource indexes. ([pls-lab.org](https://www.pls-lab.org/en/Classic_Papers_in_PL)) It was also discussed on Hacker News in December 2013, indicating circulation among software developers. ([news.ycombinator.com](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=6852619)) No evidence was found that the page itself directly influenced subsequent research results or industry technology; its documented impact is primarily dissemination and curation of existing books and learning materials.
